newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open higher, boosted by dollar.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open higher, boosted by dollar.

text.p: French stocks opened sharply higher on Friday, bolstered by the dollar's rise to nearly 6.2 francs and a fresh record on Wall Street.
The CAC-40 index was up 32.53 points, or 1.09 percent, at 3,006.06 at 0822 GMT. It hit an early high of 3,024.10, just shy of the 3,026.99 record.
The CAC-40 July futures contract was trading at 3,000, up 21 from Thursday's close.
The broader SBF120 index was up 20.88 points at 2,049.68.
Rhone-Poulenc shares were up 2.54 percent at 254.80 francs after the chemicals group reported a 20.2 percent rise in second-quarter net income. Brokers said the results were excellent.
PSA Peugeot Citroen was the top gainer on the CAC, rising 3.55 percent to 671 francs, helped by recent recommendations on the French car sector.
Brokers say the stock breached key resistance levels and is now bumping up against one at 675 francs.

They say Peugeot is catching up with Renault's recent rally. One broker said the Peugeot group is likely to benefit more than Renault from positive foreign exchange movements, notably sterling's rise.
LVMH performed in line with the market even though Guinness and GrandMet flatly rejected its proposal for a three-way drinks merger.

"We're going to war," said one broker. But he said the market was confident in LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault, who is trying to line up enough support among GrandMet shareholders to stop the Guinness-GrandMet merger.
